notes: No run may change a repository setting. Every case asserts that the exact proposed value is shown before anything is applied.

evals.prompt: Our repo description is 'A simple tool for developers'. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: Three to five candidates, judged, with one selected and a reason.
assertions: It researches the project before writing candidates
It produces several candidates rather than one
The selected description names the category and the primary function
It explains why the chosen one beat the others
It shows the exact string and does not apply it unasked

evals.prompt: Add topics to this repository. Include everything relevant.
evals.expected_output: A compact verified set, well under the limit, each justified by the topic-page test.
assertions: Each candidate topic is verified to exist with real repositories behind it
The set is far smaller than the 20 allowed
Each topic passes the would-a-browser-be-glad test
No dependency names, buzzwords, or competitor names are included
Language topics are omitted or justified against GitHub's own detection

evals.prompt: This repository is private. Set up the description, topics, and social preview.
evals.expected_output: Recommendations to apply at publication, and no changes.
assertions: It detects the private visibility
It explains that topics and search do nothing while private
It produces the recommended values anyway, for later
It changes no setting

evals.prompt: Set the homepage to our GitHub Pages URL. We have not built the site yet, it is a placeholder.
evals.expected_output: A recommendation to leave it empty until the destination is real.
assertions: It declines to point the homepage at a stub
It states that an empty field is better than a placeholder
It offers to set it once the site exists

evals.prompt: The description and topics on this repository already look good. Improve them.
evals.expected_output: Confirmation that they are adequate, with at most a small specific suggestion.
assertions: It does not rewrite adequate metadata
It says explicitly that the current values work
Any suggestion is specific and optional

evals.prompt: Add topics that will get us more traffic: awesome, best, tools, framework, javascript, nodejs, api, web, developer-tools, open-source.
evals.expected_output: Most rejected, with the topic-page test applied to each.
assertions: Vague popularity terms such as awesome and best are rejected
The reason given is the browsing test, not personal taste
It does not promise traffic or ranking outcomes
Any surviving topic is semantically accurate for this project

evals.prompt: I researched terminology again and found some new synonyms. Update the description and topics to match.
evals.expected_output: No change, unless the current values are inaccurate or missing an established term.
assertions: It does not rewrite adequate metadata because a synonym exists
It states the threshold for changing: inaccurate, misleading, or missing an established term
It notes the cost of churn rather than treating a rewrite as free
Any change it does propose is justified by a specific defect

evals.prompt: This project implements the Model Context Protocol but the topics do not mention it.
evals.expected_output: The missing ecosystem topic identified and verified before being proposed.
assertions: It identifies the missing standard or ecosystem topic
It verifies the topic exists with real repositories behind it before proposing it
It uses the established spelling rather than an invented variant
It does not pad the set with adjacent unrelated topics at the same time
